children: Seer reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $4.0 million, down 3% from a year earlier, and a net loss of $13.7 million. The company ended the quarter with $198.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments, and lowered its full-year revenue guidance to $13.5 million–$14.5 million.
Revenue was $3.981 million, compared with $4.121 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Gross profit was $1.879 million, with a gross margin of 47%.
Operating expenses were $16.546 million, compared with $21.456 million in the prior-year quarter; loss from operations was $14.667 million.
Net loss was $13.738 million, compared with $18.234 million a year earlier. Basic and diluted net loss per share was $0.25.
Cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled approximately $198.1 million at quarter-end. Seer revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $13.5 million–$14.5 million from $16 million–$18 million.

Established customers continued purchasing consumables, with some accounts making purchases over multiple consecutive quarters. New pharmaceutical customers adopted the platform and purchased instruments and consumables.
Seer said ongoing pressure on academic and government funding extended sales cycles, and several late-stage opportunities were expected to close later than planned.
After a Board special committee completed its review, Seer said it would remain an independent public company.

In the ITC proceeding brought by Seer and Brigham and Women’s Hospital, investigative staff recommended the requested exclusion and cease-and-desist orders after Nanomics Biotechnology withdrew from defending the investigation. The Commission’s final determination was pending and expected by year-end.

Research publications, preprints and reviews using Proteograph reached 116. Presentations and studies highlighted its use in population-scale proteomics, plasma protein coverage and AI-based cancer classification.
